history.summary: THIS IS A BIRD SANCTUARY, NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — the CSV row name 'Uppalapadu Bird Sanctuary Temple' is a misnomer; there is no temple here. Keep-or-drop decision needed. The sanctuary is the village water tanks of Uppalapadu near Guntur, a heronry used for nesting by spot-billed pelicans, painted storks, Asian openbills, black-headed ibises and other waterbirds migrating from Siberia, Australia and elsewhere. Bird counts were around 12,000 historically and roughly 7,000 in recent years, with pelican numbers above 1,500. The Forest Department has added artificial wire-mesh nesting trees, improved water supply and run local awareness programs; the pelicanary has operated as a managed site since the 2000s. There is a small watchtower for viewing and photography.

town_description: Uppalapadu is a village near Guntur city in Guntur district, Andhra Pradesh (in the Pedakakani area). Its only claim to fame is the village-tank bird sanctuary that has become a nesting colony for thousands of pelicans and painted storks.
